issues.description: Method parameter type mismatch for Pneumatic.raisePressure: the UML in the problem statement declares raisePressure(pressureIncrease: int) (problem_statement.md), but the reference implementation's Pneumatic interface declares raisePressure(double pressureIncrease) (solution_repository/src/de/tum/in/ase/Pneumatic.java line 5). Additionally, the concrete classes in the solution (LaunchedDropdownTower and LaunchedRollerCoaster) implement raisePressure with an int parameter (solution_repository/src/de/tum/in/ase/LaunchedDropdownTower.java and .../LaunchedRollerCoaster.java line 10), so the interface and implementations disagree. This inconsistency will cause compilation errors or confuse students about the correct signature to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the parameter type for Pneumatic.raisePressure across all artifacts. Preferred action: change the Pneumatic interface in the solution and the template to declare void raisePressure(int pressureIncrease) (update solution_repository/src/de/tum/in/ase/Pneumatic.java line 5 and add the same signature in template_repository/src/de/tum/in/ase/Pneumatic.java). Ensure all implementing classes use the same int parameter and update any tests or documentation accordingly. Alternatively, if double was intended, update the UML/problem statement and all implementing classes to use double consistently.
